content:
alex: Heads-up — we need to expose quantization knobs in the SDK before the next Dedicated rollout. Main asks: presets, safety rails, and a clear migration note for FP8/INT8/4-bit.

lin: totally. we have profiling data showing FP8 gives ~2.2x throughput vs fp16 on short sequences but degrades quality for long contexts unless calibrated. INT8 is safer: ~1.8x and small quality delta after per-channel calibration. 4-bit is tricky — big memory win but kernel math/packing slows us on some HW.

jo: kernel selection needs to be dynamic. current heuristic picks kernels by model size only; we should consider seqlen distribution + kv-cache hit rate. mixing quant modes in the same batch causes slow paths (dequant/requant). propose: choose per-request kernel and refuse mixed-mode batches unless all requests set quant=auto and we do on-the-fly fallback.

maya: for SDK params I'm thinking: `quant.mode` (auto|fp16|int8|fp8|q4), `quant.preset` (latency|accuracy|balanced), `quant.calibration` (none|per_layer|per_channel|auto), `quant.safety.fail_on_quality_drop` (true|false). examples?

alex: good. also need clear defaults so self-serve users don't shoot themselves. default: `quant.mode=auto`, `preset=balanced`, `calibration=auto`, `safety.fail_on_quality_drop=true`?

lin: agree on defaults. note: `calibration=auto` will run a fast 1-2 batch calibration in the background for int8/fp8 when model is first served; if it fails we fallback to fp16 and log a metric. should expose that metric.

sam: question on KV cache — does quantized kernel keep KV in quantized format? cache coherency/IO cost matters for long contexts.

lin: good call. current prototype keeps KV in quantized form for int8/q4 and only dequantizes when needed for attention matmul. that saves memory but introduces dequant cost per request. for high KV hit rates (many continuation tokens) we saw net win; for streaming random-access patterns dequant cost dominates.

jo: that's why kernel selection should look at `kv_cache_hit_rate` and `avg_continuation_len`. if kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.6 and continuation_len > 64 then prefer quant kernels; else prefer fp16. we can add those as runtime signals.

perf-bot: automated profile run 2024-10-03T11:12Z: model=redwood-13b, hw=A100-80G, seq=2048->512, batch=8: fp16=baseline, int8=+1.9x tokens/s, fp8=+2.3x tokens/s but +9% ppl on evaluation set, q4=+2.6x tokens/s but instability on layernorm observed.

maya: can we include a short SDK snippet for docs? something like:```python
client.generate(
  model="redwood-13b",
  prompt=prompt,
  quant={
    "mode": "auto",
    "preset": "balanced",
    "calibration": "auto",
    "safety": {"fail_on_quality_drop": True}
  }
)
```

alex: yes — but we must call out caveats: FP8 requires calibration and may be disabled in Private deployments without the calibration microservice. also call out GPU compatibility matrix.

lin: action items: (1) runtime: add heuristics for seqlen+kv hit routing and disallow mixed-quant batches by default. (2) ml: add quick per-channel calibration path + metric emission. (3) devex: draft SDK param surface + migration guide and compatibility table. (4) docs: add examples and a 'when not to use quant' section.

maya: I'll draft SDK docs + examples. can someone paste the HW compatibility table and the perf CSV?

jo: attaching quick notes (paste): `A100: int8/fp8/q4 supported but q4 slow on older drivers; H100: fp8 supported, q4 good; T4/RTX: only int8 stable.`

lin: perf CSV (snippet): `mode,seq,rate,quality_delta
fp16,512,100,0
int8,512,190,-0.8
fp8,512,230,-6.7
q4,512,260,-12.5`

sam: OK — thanks. last question: do we want an opt-in 'aggressive' preset that tries fp8/q4 and logs fallback reason? useful for benchmarking customers.

alex: yes add `preset=aggressive` but require `safety.fail_on_quality_drop=false` to enable. also expose `quant.debug.trace` for internal runs.

maya: will include all that and a short migration checklist. ping me if you want to review PR. :thumbsup:

alex: awesome, let's track in the runtime-quant epic and assign tasks. thanks everyone.
